merged.title: perf(enhanced): faster Enhanced graphics on handhelds, presets and effects detail
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before**
Enhanced graphics took about 27.6 ms of GPU a frame on the Odin 3 at preset Low with upscaling, and 16.7 ms at native 1080p (base game: 4.4 to 5.7 ms). Quality options mostly scaled resolution, and phones started on the PC defaults.

**After**
Measured on the Odin 3 (Novalis, standing):
- Upscaling Performance, Low: 27.6 -> about 12.2 ms. Native 1080p, Low, no AA: 16.7 -> 14.2 ms.
- Mode uniforms become pipeline specialisation constants, so the driver drops the code a mode leaves out (about 4.8 ms).
- Paths only a few draws need left every world shader: leaf back shadow, fur and wet coat outside Ratchet, cheaper probe light for blended mobys, a lighter early-lighting read.
- New setting Effects detail, set by the presets. High has no lossy shortcut. Medium and Low allow coarser water, cheaper blended light and far shadows in turns. Low also does early GI on 4x4 cells and one far cascade a frame.
- Sharper upscaler: ASR quality shaders and a mip bias while the world is drawn

merged.title: build(port): include <chrono> where mods.cpp reads the steady clock
merged.author: farfeduc
merged.untrustedBody:
`port/game/common/mods.cpp` calls `std::chrono::steady_clock::now()` without including `<chrono>`. With libc++ on Windows (llvm-mingw, clang 23) no other header brings it in, so `openrac_mods` does not build there:

```
mods.cpp:210:49: error: no member named 'steady_clock' in namespace 'std::chrono'
```

One line: `#include <chrono>` beside the other standard headers.

## Verified

- `openrac_mods` and the mod tests (`mod_loader`, `mod_manifest`, `mod_scripts`, `settings`, `mod_ui_menus`, `mod_touch`, `mod_boundary`) build and pass with llvm-mingw (clang 23) on Windows, configured with `cmake --preset release`.

## Not verified

- Not built with MSVC, GCC or Apple clang here (the include is standard and changes nothing where it already built).

#459 and #460 carry this same commit as their first, since they build `mods.cpp`; once this one is in, they rebase to their own commit.

merged.author: nickyyOO

## Before

SDR clips each channel at white, so stacked fire sprites look orange. HDR keeps the mix, so the same fire looks red (3 layers: OKLab hue 109° in SDR, 47° in HDR). Players who use RenoDX asked for an "SDR Hue" slider.

## After

Four sliders in Graphics > HDR (desktop menu and Android drawer; mouse, touch and pad) and in the settings file:

- **SDR hue** (`hdr_sdr_hue`, default 0): very bright colours take their SDR hue.
- **SDR chrominance** (`hdr_sdr_chroma`, default 0): and their SDR saturation.
- **HDR highlights** (`hdr_highlights`, default 100): 0 is as in SDR.
- **HDR blowout** (`hdr_blowout`, default 0): very bright light fades to white.

Only pixels above white change. The defaults keep today's picture bit for bit.

- `common/hdr.h` (`to_light`, `apply_look`) and `hdr_encode.comp` do the same math. Hue and saturation mix in OKLab; lightness stays HDR's. A colour outside BT.709 moves towards grey until it fits. It never passes the peak.

This addresses the failure mechanism investigated for support ticket T-15: Multiplayer was refused after Weapon Wheel Pause had acquired the gate, followed by a crash opening the Novalis vendor. The affected code is identical in reported build `117cc13f` and current develop `c381cf6ed`. merged.title: fix(index): bind a review approval to the archives' SHA-256
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
A maintainer approved a version by its number only. The author could replace a release archive after the review, and the index then published the new, unreviewed file.

## After
The approval stores the SHA-256 of each archive shown on the review issue. If an archive changes, that version waits for review again. The bot reopens the closed issue (or warns on the open one) and removes the `approved` label.

## How
- `submit_bot.py review` writes the hashes on the issue's last line. Only that line counts, so hashes in the author's changelog are ignored.
- `submit_bot.py approve` saves `{version, sha256}` in `index/approved.json`.
- `build_index.py` publishes only when the release's hashes match. Older entries with a bare version still work.

## Tested
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/tests`: 108 tests pass (7 new).
- `python3 tools/build_index.py --check --offline tools/tests/fixtures/github` passes.
- Not tested: the workflows on GitHub.
